items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: I played with guys like Bill...I can't think of Bill's name right... Bill Douglas, played bass.

ctx.x: dice. And we were over there playing music with a trio or duo.

I played with guys like Bill...I can't think of Bill's name right... Bill Douglas, played bass. He fists the bass. He never played a note on the bass yet. He just fists the bass and plays and smiles. And some of them Italians know music; they know that he ain't playin' nothin'. But they like him for his gayness(?). See, racketeers love you for your gayness. And they'd say, "Go and play us a solo, Bill." And he's just fistin' the bass. The bass ain't even in tune. And I'm playing. Now, to conquer him, I say, "Now,…

Curly Russell... We were working a joint in the Bronx. Curly Russell came over and looked at me on the stand with Bill. There was two of us playing this little joint. The Italians love him. Over there is a big old crate of lamb heads. First time I've seen it. This is real mafia, in the Bronx. Lamb skull. You know the skulls?
